question: A complete written rheumatologic assessment must include the distribution and symmetry of joint involvement, the inflammatory vs mechanical pattern, any systemic features, and the working differential diagnosis — all before ordering investigations.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is TRUE. Rheumatologic documentation should capture the pattern (mono/oligo/poly, symmetric/asymmetric), inflammatory vs mechanical categorisation, systemic features, and working differential before tests are ordered — mirroring the 'hypothesis-first' principle of investigation.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. The clinical documentation in rheumatology follows a structured sequence: history (pattern of joint involvement, inflammatory vs mechanical features, systemic review), examination findings, working differential, and then targeted investigation selection. This 'hypothesis first' approach prevents inappropriate blanket autoimmune panel ordering.
